newsitem.title: CHINA: China slams Latin America over Taiwan WHO bid.
newsitem.headline: China slams Latin America over Taiwan WHO bid.

text.p: China on Tuesday attacked a motion by some Latin American countries backing a request by Taiwan to join the World Health Organisation (WHO), and hailed the U.N. agency's rejection of Taiwan's bid.

"Under any pretext to put forward the issue of Taiwan representation in the WHO is to brazenly create two Chinas or one China, one Taiwan," Foreign Minstry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a regular news briefing.
"This seriously violates China's sovereignty and wantonly interferes in China's internal affairs, the Chinese government and people cannot tolerate it," Cui said.

WHO Director-General Hiroshi Nakajima last Thursday rejected Taiwan's request for observer status, saying its application was controversial and a United Nations General Assembly resolution of 1971 transferred China's U.N. seat from Taipei to Beijing.
"The WHO's position is clear and persistent, we express our appreciation for this," Cui said.

China, which has regarded Taiwan as a rebel-held province ineligible for international recognition since a civil war split them in 1949, has blocked Taipei's membership as a sovereign state in all international forums since taking the U.N. seat.
"Taiwan, as a province of China, has no such qualification," Cui said.

Taiwan said last Wednesday it had applied to become an observer at WHO and urged Beijing not to block its bid to take part in what Foreign Minister John Chang called the least politically sensitive U.N. body.
